sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento del VIX del 39.68% e della chiusura negativa dei mercati azionari nella sessione precedente. L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo del 2.64%, mentre il DXY è salito dello 0.66%. Il prezzo del petrolio è sceso del 2.04%, mentre l'oro è calato del 3.10%.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the 39.68% increase in VIX and the negative close of equity markets in the previous session. S&P 500 fell 2.64%, while DXY rose 0.66%. Oil prices dropped 2.04%, and gold declined 3.10%.

market_impact_summary.it: Nella sessione precedente, i mercati azionari hanno chiuso in calo, con l'S&P 500 in perdita del 2.64%. Il VIX è salito del 39.68%, raggiungendo 21.51. Il DXY è aumentato dello 0.66%, mentre il prezzo del petrolio è sceso del 2.04%. L'oro ha perso il 3.10%.
market_impact_summary.en: In the previous session, equity markets closed lower, with S&P 500 down 2.64%. VIX surged 39.68% to 21.51. DXY rose 0.66%, while oil prices fell 2.04%. Gold declined 3.10%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso in territorio negativo: il Nikkei ha perso l'1.31%, Shanghai l'0.74%, e l'Hang Seng l'1.15%.

Mentre le borse mondiali osservano la consueta pausa festiva, i riflettori restano accesi sul quadro macroeconomico. Nella seduta precedente, S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo del 2.64%, il VIX è schizzato del 39.68%, segnale di crescente avversione al rischio. L'oro è sceso a $4337.1/oncia, in calo del 3.1%, e il petrolio Brent ha perso il 2.04%, quotato a $93.09

Sul fronte geopolitico, si segnalano le tensioni in Ucraina con significative sfide fiscali e finanziarie, e la crisi nello stretto di Hormuz che evidenzia la strategia petrolifera unica della Cina. La BCE valuta un aumento dei tassi in un'economia gradualmente in rallentamento.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi, in quanto i mercati tradizionali sono chiusi per il fine settimana.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin scende del 2,58% a sessantunomila centouno dollari. I flussi netti negli ETF Bitcoin sono stati positivi per 3,2 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dinamiche di mercato.

Anche le altcoin mostrano perdite: Ethereum scende del 5,43% a millecinquecentosettantasette dollari, Solana del 4,22% a sessantadue virgola ottantaquattro dollari e BNB del 1,45% a cinquecentosettantanove virgola novantacinque dollari.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 12, in zona di Extreme Fear, il che suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. Asian markets closed in negative territory: Nikkei lost 1.31%, Shanghai 0.74%, and Hang Seng 1.15%. While global stock markets observe the usual festive pause, the spotlight remains on the macroeconomic picture. In the previous session, S&P 500 closed down 2.64%, VIX jumped 39.68%, a sign of growing risk aversion. Gold fell to $4337.1/oz, down 3.1%, and Brent crude oil lost 2.04%, quoted at $93.09 On the geopolitical front, tensions in Ukraine with significant fiscal and financial challenges, and the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz highlight China's unique oil strategy. The ECB considers raising rates in a gradually slowing economy. No major macroeconomic data due today, as traditional markets are closed for the weekend. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin falls 2.58% to $61,001 Net flows into Bitcoin ETFs were positive at $3.2 million. This move could be influenced by recent market dynamics. Altcoins also show losses: Ethereum down 5.43% to $1,577, Solana 4.22% to $62.84, and BNB 1.45% to $559.95 The Fear & Greed Index is at 12, in Extreme Fear territory, suggesting investor caution. No macroeconomic data on the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
articles.snippet: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

articles.summary_en: The author argues that the ECB should not raise interest rates until there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched.

articles.title: Ukraine's fiscal and financial challenges
articles.snippet: As it faces the exigencies of an existential war, Ukraine is confronted with stark fiscal and financial policy trade-offs, despite the mitigation provided by large-scale external financial support. So far, its authorities have kept monetary and financial stability under control beyond a relatively brief initial episode of turmoil in 2022. What is the broad fiscal equation for Ukraine looking forward, taking into account uncertainties about European funding beyond 2027? Can domestic revenue be raised? articles.title: When Markets Run on Empty
articles.snippet: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

articles.title: Bank of England Official Says Oil Crisis Clouds Rate Outlook
articles.snippet: The Bank of England may know where inflation is headed, but it has a much harder time knowing where oil—and interest rates—are headed. That was the message from Bank of England policymaker Swati Dhingra on Friday, as the ongoing Middle East energy crisis continues to complicate the outlook for interest rates. "If you ask me what's my interest rate decision next month going to look like or in the future, I think that's very hard to say, because the big elephant in the room here is what happens to the energy crisis," Dhingra said during…

articles.title: EU Says No Jet Fuel Shortage Coming Despite Middle East Supply Loss
articles.snippet: Shortages of jet fuel are not looming over Europe despite the shock loss of supply from the Middle East and soaring prices, according to EU Sustainable Transport and Tourism Commissioner, Apostolos Tzitzikostas. “There is currently no jet fuel shortage in Europe. We have no signs that we will have a shortage in the coming period,” Tzitzikostas told Reuters in an interview published on Friday. Since the war in Iran broke out on February 28, European airlines have been struggling with a spike in jet fuel prices, while officials and analysts…
